texts.preamble: Dudyala Siva Kumar vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 14 August, 2019 Author: U. Durga Prasad Rao Bench: U. Durga Prasad Rao Hon'Ble Sri Justice U. Durga Prasad Rao Criminal Petition No.4831 Of 2019 Order:
texts.facts: The petitioner/accused seeks to quash the proceedings against him in Crime No.165 of 2019 of Kalasapadu Police Station, YSR Kadapa District, which was registered against him for the offence under Sections 328 and 273 of IPC and Section 5 r/w Section 22 of Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Act, 2003 (for short, 'COTP Act, 2003'). 2. The allegations against the petitioner briefly are that on 07.08.2019 at 05.00 P.M., the complainant on receiving the credible information proceeded to C.S.I. Church, near Telugu Ganga Bridge, Kalasapadu Town and Mandal, YSR Kadapa District and caught the petitioner who tried to escape along with his bag from the said place on seeing them. On his revelation, they came to know that he was selling the Gutka Packets by purchasing the same from the State of Karnataka and therefore, they arrested the accused. Hence, the FIR is registered for the offences under Sections 328 and 273 of IPC and Section 5 r/w Section 22 of COTP Act, 2003.
texts.arguments: 3. Learned counsel for petitioner while denying the FIR allegations would submit that even if the prosecution case is accepted to be true, the Gutka which is a tobacco product would not fall within the definition of Section 3(j) of Food Safety Standards Act (for short, 'FSS Act') and therefore, the police are not authorized to register the crime and investigate and file charge sheet and therefore, registration of the FIR is contrary to the provisions of FSS Act.
texts.petitioner_arguments: 3. Learned counsel for petitioner while denying the FIR allegations would submit that even if the prosecution case is accepted to be true, the Gutka which is a tobacco product would not fall within the definition of Section 3(j) of Food Safety Standards Act (for short, 'FSS Act') and therefore, the police are not authorized to register the crime and investigate and file charge sheet and therefore, registration of the FIR is contrary to the provisions of FSS Act.
